cutoff_window.rule: Only public sources visibly published or updated inside this seven-day window qualify; missing, ambiguous, future, and boundary-only dates are excluded.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: visible publication date on source page
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Snowflake describes enterprise MCP gateway governance as a control plane for agent-to-system traffic, emphasizing dynamic user-delegated identity, tool-parameter-level policies, cataloged approved tools, cost guardrails, and audit logs that preserve agent intent, tool choices, and blocked attempts. It cites August 2026 enterprise earnings-call signals for rapid MCP growth at Datadog, Figma, Atlassian, and Salesforce.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds practice evidence that governed agent access must move from endpoint authorization to per-tool, per-parameter, per-user, trajectory-audited control, reinforcing local database access and outcome-evidence boundaries.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Consider adding MCP gateway trajectory and identity-bound audit evidence to governed database access and trajectory-level eval leaves during ingest.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: visible byline date on source page
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CData frames AI agent data governance around what data an agent can access, what actions it can take, and how those actions are attributed. It recommends named source owners, sensitivity classification, lineage, access policy, retention policy, least privilege, identity passthrough, workspace isolation, and SIEM-exportable audit trails.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Strengthens the local rule that enterprise data tools need source ownership, identity-bound permissions, workspace isolation, and reconstructable audit evidence before agents query or mutate business systems.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest with vendor-positioning caveat; route product detail upstream and keep source-level readiness and audit criteria locally.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: WIRED reports that Meta reduced performance-review language tied to AI usage and token consumption while encouraging employees to test Hatch, an agentic tool that can browse the web and operate applications. Employees raised privacy, resource-use, and bug concerns; Meta stated that contribution impact, not AI adoption dashboards or token counts, is the evaluation focus.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds current operating-model evidence against measuring AI adoption by token volume or tool-use dashboards and for judging agent use by accepted contribution impact, privacy posture, resource burden, and defect outcomes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Fold into outcome alignment and hybrid economics; avoid duplicating Meta/Hatch product coverage locally.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: visible publication date on source page
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar summarizes Decodo research evaluating 45 AI agents across 10 autonomous browsing capabilities. No agent achieved a perfect score; transaction handling was the weakest category, and more than half of agents capable of multi-step workflows lacked documented safeguards before irreversible actions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds browser-agent eval evidence that local verification should test transaction completion, cross-tab awareness, third-party integration behavior, and safeguards before irreversible actions, not only vendor claims.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as browser-agent verification and trajectory evidence; route product rankings upstream.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: visible publication date on source page
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI describes Astra-class cybersecurity capability evaluation and production misalignment monitoring, including classifiers that inspect reasoning and actions for unauthorized behavior and stop or pause tasks. It notes that legitimate long-running work may be slowed, paused, or stopped when safeguards flag potential misuse.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds current safety-eval evidence for long-running, high-capability agents: local evals should preserve action trajectories, pause reasons, human review points, and false-positive calibration for consequential tasks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep model and benchmark cataloging upstream; ingest only the local monitor, pause, and calibration implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Cloudflare announced support for running Cursor Cloud Agents on Cloudflare Sandboxes. Cursor keeps the agent loop, routing, and result streaming, while terminal, filesystem, and browser actions run on a customer-controlled worker or sandbox; repositories, build caches, and secrets remain on customer machines, while chunks and artifacts may be uploaded for PR and dashboard views.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds concrete portability and economics evidence that self-hosted execution can be separated from provider-hosted planning, orchestration, inference, artifacts, and dashboards; local reviews should track which layer actually moved.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use for managed-agent portability and hybrid infrastructure economics; route product background upstream.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: visible journal date on source page
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CODERCOPS describes spec-driven development as making a written spec the artifact an AI agent builds from, with requirements, technical design, and task breakdown reviewed before implementation. It warns that specs drift when treated as one-time ritual rather than living source-of-truth material.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds current PRD/spec practice evidence that agent-readable specs need reviewable requirements, technical design, acceptance criteria, task breakdowns, versioning, and drift controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest into executable PRD templates with source-quality caveat; treat tool comparisons as upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: A Python in Plain English article argues that developers increasingly direct, review, and validate AI coding agents rather than only writing code, citing asynchronous GitHub coding agents and longer-running Codex-style engineering tasks as examples.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Adds a lightweight practice signal for preserving developer learning around directing, reviewing, validating, and debugging agent work rather than only accepting generated code.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use cautiously because the page is member-only and gives a relative date; prefer stronger corroboration during ingest.
